questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, your lane position:

options.text: Does not affect whether other drivers can see you.
Is very important because it affects whether other drivers can see you.
Cannot protect you from wind blasts from other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is very important because it affects whether other drivers can see you.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps other drivers see you. It also helps you avoid wind blasts from other vehicles.

questions.question: A flat front tire is especially dangerous because:

options.text: The front tire controls your steering, which affects your balance.
A flat front tire will disable your front brake.
A flat front tire will stop you from accelerating.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front tire controls your steering, which affects your balance.
questions.explanation: A flat front tire is dangerous because it makes steering difficult. This affects your balance. If steering feels heavy, you may have a flat front tire.

questions.question: To stop quickly, you should:

options.text: Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, use both brakes at the same time.

questions.question: What should you do if you must ride on a slippery surface?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, reduce your speed, avoid sudden movements, and use both brakes.

questions.question: A benefit of keeping space between you and other vehicles is that:

options.text: You can draft off other vehicles more easily.
You will be able to stop quickly.
You will have more time to react to other drivers' movements.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will have more time to react to other drivers' movements.
questions.explanation: Keep space around your motorcycle at all times. This gives you time to respond to hazards and space to maneuver safely.

questions.question: When a tailgater is following you, you should:

options.text: Change lanes to let them pass or slow down to create more space.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes to let them pass or slow down to create more space.
questions.explanation: Ride in a way that encourages a tailgater to pass. Speeding up will only make them tailgate you at higher speeds, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: When starting your motorcycle, the engine should be in:
questions.correctAnswerText: Neutral.
questions.explanation: Start your motorcycle with the transmission in neutral. Most motorcycles have a light on the speedometer that shows when the engine is in neutral.

questions.question: Reflective clothing:

options.text: Should be worn only at night.
Should be worn only during the day.
Should be worn day and night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be worn day and night.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wear bright, reflective clothing at all times, day or night.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They warn you about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that the road will be slippery when wet.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Vehicles will enter the roadway ahead.
Come to a complete stop and go when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are always stop signs. You must come to a complete stop, look for other traffic or pedestrians, and go when it is safe.

questions.question: A good lane position should:

options.text: Help you see others and be seen.
Place you in other drivers' blind spots.
Invite other drivers to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you see others and be seen.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see others and lets them see you. It keeps you away from wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. It also stops other drivers from sharing your lane and gives you room to escape if danger appears.

questions.question: Should you wear gloves while riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Yes. Your hands may get cold while riding.
Yes. They give you a better grip and protect your hands.
No. Gloves can get in the way of the controls.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes. They give you a better grip and protect your hands.
questions.explanation: Gloves give you a better grip and protect your hands while riding. Use gloves that cover all fingers and are made of strong material.

questions.question: If vehicles are on both sides of your motorcycle, which lane position is usually best?
questions.correctAnswerText: Center
questions.explanation: No lane position is always best or always bad. Good riders change their position based on road and traffic conditions. When vehicles are on both sides, the center position is usually safest.

questions.question: When riding in a group, mirrors should:

options.text: Be checked often by all riders.
Be used only by the lead rider.
Not be checked often because they distract you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be checked often by all riders.
questions.explanation: When riding in a group, check your mirrors often to watch the riders behind you and make sure the group stays together.

questions.question: Riding boots or shoes should:

options.text: Be made of soft, flexible material.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover your ankles.
questions.explanation: For riding, wear sturdy shoes that cover and support your ankles. The soles should be made of hard, durable material that resists slipping.

questions.question: Riding right after rain starts is difficult because:

options.text: Other drivers may not react quickly to the rain.
Other drivers do not drive fast enough in wet weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: The pavement becomes very slippery.
questions.explanation: When rain first starts, the pavement is very slippery. Oil from vehicles has not yet washed away, and it mixes with water to create a slick surface.

questions.question: Wind noise while riding:

options.text: Is easy to get used to.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can permanently damage your hearing.
questions.explanation: Long-term exposure to wind noise can permanently damage your hearing. Use proper ear plugs or hearing protection when riding.

questions.question: You should check your motorcycle's safety before riding:
questions.correctAnswerText: Before every ride.
questions.explanation: Always check your motorcycle's safety before every ride. Small problems on a motorcycle are more dangerous than small problems on a car.

questions.question: A solid white line on the side of the road means:

options.text: The right edge of a traffic lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right edge of a traffic lane.
questions.explanation: A solid white line on the side of the road marks the right edge of a traffic lane.

questions.question: If you must stop quickly, you should:

options.text: Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: The best way to stop quickly is to press both the rear and front brakes at the same time with controlled pressure. Do not lock the brakes.

questions.question: Which item is NOT recommended as protective gear for motorcycle riders?
questions.correctAnswerText: A baseball cap
questions.explanation: Wear protective gear when riding a motorcycle. Good protective clothing includes long-sleeved jackets, long heavy pants, closed-toe boots, and full-fingered leather gloves. Cover as much skin as possible.

questions.question: White lines separate traffic that moves in the same direction. What do different types of white lines mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: White lines.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. Solid white lines mean you cannot pass. Dashed white lines mean you can pass if it is safe.

questions.question: Which color makes you less visible to other drivers?
questions.correctAnswerText: Brown
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors like orange, red, yellow, or green to be more visible. Avoid dark or dull colors while riding.

questions.question: What is a sign that your rear tire has gone flat?

options.text: The back of your motorcycle sways from side to side.

questions.correctAnswerText: The back of your motorcycle sways from side to side.
questions.explanation: If your rear tire goes flat, the back of the motorcycle may jerk or sway side to side. If you feel this movement, stop and check your tires right away.

questions.question: When should you NOT flash your brake light?

options.text: When you are slowing down faster than others expect
When you are slowing down where others won't expect it
When people are walking on a nearby sidewalk

questions.correctAnswerText: When people are walking on a nearby sidewalk
questions.explanation: Flash your brake light to warn other drivers. A motorcycle brake light is less noticeable than a car's. Flash it before slowing where drivers may not expect it or when slowing faster than normal.

questions.question: What is true about a DOT-approved helmet?

options.text: It lets you see as far to the sides as you need for safe riding.
It can become a hazard to the rider.

questions.correctAnswerText: It lets you see as far to the sides as you need for safe riding.
questions.explanation: A DOT-approved helmet does not limit your vision. You can see as far as you need for safe riding.

questions.question: Which material offers the best crash protection?
questions.correctAnswerText: Leather or synthetic materials
questions.explanation: Leather and synthetic materials offer the best crash protection. Always wear long pants and jackets while riding.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection, where should you position your motorcycle in the lane?

options.text: In the part of the lane where other drivers can see you most easily.
In the part closest to the traffic control device.
On the outside edge of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the part of the lane where other drivers can see you most easily.
questions.explanation: Move to the part of the lane that puts you in another driver's field of vision as early as possible.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle
questions.explanation: This sign is on the back of slow-moving vehicles going under 25 mph, such as farm equipment, construction vehicles, or horse-drawn wagons.

questions.question: What is true about improper braking on a motorcycle?

options.text: It is a major cause of motorcycle crashes.
It should not be a concern since motorcycles have two brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is a major cause of motorcycle crashes.
questions.explanation: Improper braking causes many motorcycle crashes. Learning proper braking technique is essential for safe riding.
